sentences.text: Eoraptor was a small, lightly built basal sauropodomorph dinosaur that measured about one meter in length and stood roughly 30 centimeters tall.
Known specimens measure between 1.2 and 1.3 meters long and weigh around or less than 10 kilograms.
The name Eoraptor translates to 'dawn plunderer', referencing its primitive nature and presumed carnivorous habits with a grasping hand.

The generic name combines the Greek word 'Eo' meaning early and the Latin 'raptor' meaning thief, while the species name lunensis derives from the Latin 'luna' meaning moon and the suffix '-ensis' meaning inhabitant.
The generic name Eoraptor combines the Greek word 'Eo' meaning early and the Latin 'raptor' meaning thief.
The species name lunensis derives from the Latin 'luna' meaning moon and the suffix '-ensis' meaning inhabitant.
The bones of Eoraptor were first discovered in 1991 by paleontologists Ricardo Martínez and Paul Sereno.
Scientists began analyzing the bones of this dinosaur in 1993, dating it to 228 million years ago.
Eoraptor possessed multiple tooth shapes, suggesting it was an omnivore.
Eoraptor likely fed on reptiles, small mammals, and insects.
Eoraptor was a swift sprinter that used claws and teeth to tear apart prey after catching it.
Unlike later carnivorous dinosaurs, Eoraptor lacked a sliding joint in its lower jaw, limiting its ability to hold large prey.
Its jaws possessed very varied teeth, some sharp for cutting meat like carnosaurs, others curved for crushing plants like sauropods, and some leaf-shaped for stripping branches like ornithopods.
Eoraptor had a dental formula of 4 teeth in the premaxilla and 18 in the maxilla, similar to that of Herrerasaurus.
The classification of Eoraptor has been unstable, with opinions varying between it being a basal saurischian or a basal theropod.
Eoraptor is classified in the Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Sauropsida, Superorder Dinosauria, Order Saurischia, Suborder Sauropodomorpha.
Eoraptor belonged to an important group of dinosaurs called saurischians.

One possibility is that it is the most basal theropod, outside a clade containing herrerasaurids and Avetheropoda, or as a sister group to the clade including sauropodomorphs and theropods, Eusaurischia.
Eoraptor lived in the Late Triassic in a warm, humid floodplain forest with seasonal heavy rainfall.
Eoraptor lived in what is now Argentina.
The time range for Eoraptor is the Carnian stage, from 233.6 to 227.3 million years ago.
Absolute dating of the rock layers allows Eoraptor to be placed among the oldest known dinosaurs.
Bonaparte interpreted the relatively large eye orbit as a juvenile trait in 1996, and Ronald Tykoski agreed in 2005 that certain skull features suggested the holotype was juvenile.
Paul Sereno and colleagues interpreted Eoraptor as an adult in 1993 based on vertebral suture closure and partial scapulocoracoid fusion.
Michael Benton expressed hesitation regarding this, stating that removing Eoraptor from Theropoda and placing it in Sauropodomorpha is 'a big change.'
